title: Whole-job billing and partition/fabric economics
summary: Dev4 whole-job model includes billing quanta/minima, startup, storage, I/O, ingress/egress, checkpoint frequency, runtime overhead and interruption provision; segmented 32+32 GiB placement requires actual Memory Fabric capacity semantics, not arithmetic on VM RAM labels.
invariants: Two 32 GiB VMs are not necessarily a contiguous 64 GiB address space.
CPU ownership, memory contributors, site locality, fabric traffic and latency must be represented separately.
Minimum billing periods and failed/abandoned restarts can reverse a nominal per-hour price ranking.
Fabrics and multi-cloud migration must include network and data-movement charges.

provenance.claim: Cloud Economics v0.1-dev8 source evidence; status=IMPLEMENTED.

procedure: Ask native Memory Fabric for executable capacity plan and provider/fragment identity.
Calculate separately each billed VM and fabric/routing component.
Compare total eligible cost with same intended outcome and quality constraints.
